articles.title: Install the server
articles.description: Install the self-hosted Log Hub server from a release Docker image and install kit, check that you are its admin, and see other ways to run it.

articles.title: Quick setup for a small team

articles.title: Install the hook
articles.description: Install, upgrade or uninstall the Log Hub telemetry hook, a Claude Code plugin that records sessions in a repository and uploads them to your server.

articles.title: Your first session
articles.description: Record your first Claude Code session with Log Hub: check the prerequisites, install the hook, run a session and explore it from the Home page.

articles.title: Connecting a Repository
articles.description: Connect a git repository to Log Hub with one install command and one config entry, confirm data flows, and fix the common problems on the way.

articles.title: Authentication modes
articles.description: Choose how people sign in to Log Hub: no password for one local user, email and password, emailed confirmation, or Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on.

articles.title: Server settings
articles.description: Configure the Log Hub server with environment variables in the install directory, from the database connection to the main options you may change.

articles.title: Tuning Your Setup
articles.description: Adjust repository settings, hook configuration and your harness based on what sessions cost and why, then compare the next sessions to close the loop.

articles.title: OTEL for organization admins
articles.description: For admins who manage Claude Code through managed settings: which telemetry keys to set so OTEL data still reaches Log Hub, and how to verify it.

articles.title: Security Hardening & Configuration
articles.description: Harden a Log Hub installation beyond a single local user: deployment checklist, authentication, TLS, data visibility, retention, backups and limits.

articles.title: All views
articles.description: Find any screen in Log Hub from one map of team, repository, session and admin views, opened with Ctrl+K and filtered by the question you have.

articles.title: Working with the Session List
articles.description: Browse the sessions of a repository: group them by branch or other modes, read each row, filter the list, stay up to date and work in team repositories.

articles.title: Session Log
articles.description: Read the full record of one Claude Code session: pick a view, move between its tabs such as Summary, Logs, Timeline and Agent Tree, and navigate within it.

articles.title: Understanding Cost & Context
articles.description: Learn how Log Hub computes session cost from token usage and model prices, where cost appears, and how context size drives the cost of every call.

articles.title: Analytics & Reports
articles.description: Explore recorded sessions with interactive Analytics charts, or share printable Reports with KPIs and trends that download as PDF for a team or management.

articles.title: OTEL tab
articles.description: Use the OTEL tabs of a session, repository or team to see what Claude Code spent per model and call source, including calls missing from transcripts.

articles.title: OTEL collection architecture
articles.description: How OpenTelemetry data travels from Claude Code through the local hook receiver to the Log Hub OTEL tabs, and why it holds up across many repositories.

articles.title: Data Collection Notice
articles.description: Read before you start: which prompts and transcripts Log Hub stores, who can see them, and how to avoid handing secrets to your AI coding assistant.

articles.title: Data Collection & Upload
articles.description: What the hook collects from your Claude Code sessions, when and how it uploads the data in the background, and how the post-turn analysis works.

articles.title: Trust model
articles.description: Who and what you trust when you run Log Hub and install its hook: the server, your API key, the installer, the hook's user rights and the local OTEL receiver.

articles.title: Component Reference
articles.description: The components of Log Hub (server, web client, PostgreSQL database, telemetry hook and installer), where each runs and how they talk to each other.

articles.title: Responsibility Matrix (RACI)
articles.description: Who is responsible for each part of running Log Hub, from releases and deployment to access, data protection and incidents: maintainers or your organisation.

articles.title: Third-Party Components
articles.description: Every third-party open-source component shipped in Log Hub, on the server, in the browser and in the hook, with its version, license and role.

articles.title: How the hook works
articles.description: Technical reference for the Log Hub hook: its configuration files, the events it records, how uploads work, its diagnostic log and how it cleans up.

articles.title: Changelog
articles.description: Find what changed in each version of Log Hub: the release notes on the releases page and the notes file shipped with every release for offline installs.
